hook: Paul Viola was born in New York City on October 22, 1966, and studied at MIT, earning a PhD in 1995 with a thesis on alignment by maximization of mutual information under advisors Christopher Atkeson and Tomas Lozano-Perez. He went on to work at MIT, the Cambridge Research Laboratory of Compaq and Hewlett Packard, and Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories before joining Microsoft Research. In 2001, with Michael Jones, he published Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features, which combined Haar like features, an integral image representation and a cascade of boosted classifiers to detect faces in video in real time. The Viola-Jones framework became the standard method for real time face detection for more than a decade and was built into consumer cameras and photo software. Viola later held research and engineering leadership roles at Microsoft, Amazon Prime Air and the self driving vehicle company Zoox, continuing to work on computer vision and machine learning problems.

moniker: Co-inventor of the Viola-Jones object detection framework

primary.name: Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features (CVPR 2001)

timeline.impact: Went on to study at MIT, where his research career began.

timeline.event: Completed his PhD at MIT with a thesis on alignment by maximization of mutual information
timeline.impact: Established his early expertise in information theoretic approaches to vision.

timeline.impact: Introduced the cascade classifier architecture that made real time face detection possible.

timeline.impact: Continued applying real time detection expertise to autonomous driving.

quick_facts: Born in New York City on October 22, 1966
Earned a PhD from MIT in 1995 under advisors Christopher Atkeson and Tomas Lozano-Perez
Co-invented the Viola-Jones framework for real time face detection with Michael Jones (2001)
Won the Longuet-Higgins Prize in 2011 for the lasting impact of the Viola-Jones paper
Holds more than 50 patents in computer vision and machine learning

achievements.title: Co-invented the Viola-Jones object detection framework
achievements.impact: Made real time face detection practical on ordinary hardware by combining Haar like features, integral images and a cascade of boosted classifiers, work later recognized with the Longuet-Higgins Prize.

achievements.title: Advanced boosting based detection methods
achievements.impact: Extended cascade classifier techniques to pedestrian detection and other real time recognition tasks.

achievements.title: Applied computer vision to autonomous systems
achievements.impact: Brought machine vision expertise to Amazon Prime Air's drone delivery program and to Zoox's self driving vehicles.
